necessary_context.content: For Q subset R^n and S subset R^m, (x*,y*) in Q×S is a saddle point if phi(x*,y)<=phi(x*,y*)<=phi(x,y*) for every y in S and x in Q. Norms and projections are Euclidean.
necessary_context.name: Saddle point

necessary_context.applies_to: Original Theorem 1 proof and interpretation of its printed step interval
necessary_context.content: Assumption b) separately bounds each partial-gradient difference by L times the product Euclidean distance. The proof defines T=(phi_x,-phi_y) and uses a joint bound with the same L in Eq.(5). These are distinct assertions; direct squared-norm aggregation gives only sqrt(2)L from the displayed block bounds.
necessary_context.locator: PDF page 3 / p.37 assumption b); PDF page 4 / p.38 Eq.(5)
necessary_context.name: Block versus joint Lipschitz constants

necessary_context.name: Projection and VI formulation
